title: Accept 30004909: An elementary obstruction to same-ground-set matroid-rank approximation
body:
## Accepted result and published preprint **An elementary obstruction to same-ground-set matroid-rank approximation**, Alec Kriebel. Published paper and verification package: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23430660 (https://zenodo.org/records/23430660).

A credited self-contained elementary exposition of the source-displayed symmetric ordinary unscaled same-ground-set matroid-rank approximation question. Inputs are nonnegative monotone submodular functions with zero empty-set value and every singleton value one. The conventional meaning of constant is taken to be dimension-independent; Végh’s complete source contribution does not separately print an all-ground-sets quantifier. Both r(S)/alpha <= f(S) <= alpha*r(S) comparisons are retained.

The classical square-root-cardinality input on n elements forces alpha >= n^(1/6). Its exact optimum among all matroids is min over integer 1<=R<=n of max(sqrt(R),sqrt(n)/R), attained by uniform ranks. On m^2 elements the rational cardinality input g(empty)=0 and g(nonempty)=1+(|S|-1)/m forces alpha^2+alpha >= m and alpha >= n^(1/4)/sqrt(2). Sharpness is only for the square-root family. Full quantified proofs and empty, singleton, loop and m=1 boundaries are included.

Credits: DDSSS 2013 Appendix D Lemma D.1 for prior uniform-rank decomposition, with corrected direct difference coefficients; classical concave-cardinality submodularity attributed by Balcan-Harvey to Lovász 1983 (original body unread); GHIM actual root-linear output and query-hard rank-input distinction; Schrijver Section 44.6b, credited there to Helgason, for expanded copied-element representation, distinct from one ordinary rank on original V (Helgason original unread). The input families and their rank-sum structure are classical. Exact one-rank argument and generic-envelope historical attribution are unresolved in the bounded review. No new-function, new-representation, firstness, intellectual-priority, independently evidenced discovery, exhaustive literature or current-worldwide-open-status claim is made. Other unread citation-chain consequences remain unknown.

Version 1.0, dated 14 October 2026. Alec Kriebel, ORCID 0009-0001-9320-500X, independent researcher, sole named author. Extensive AI assistance in solving, mathematical verification, source comparison, coding and writing. UNREFEREED: no human review, journal acceptance or formal certification. Authored exposition and code: CC BY 4.0. The supportkit preserves all nine original bodies and selected authored stage reports, checkers, output streams, pins and receipts; stage-specific AI audits and frozen inputs are identified in REVIEW_HISTORY.json and evidence/INDEX.md. The original edition had no executable; a portable adaptation of the newly authored audit checker was actually run for preparation, with no omitted historical-code replay. Finite checks supplement the written infinite proof. No third-party full bodies, extracts, images or raw/private/environment caches are redistributed. These files describe a dated local preparation stage and are not a deposit/publication record.

## Accepted scope and review No single dimension-independent alpha approximates every normalized nonnegative monotone submodular function by an ordinary matroid rank on same ground set; sqrt-cardinality forces alpha>=n^(1/6), rational family n^(1/4)/sqrt2. No gap asserted for explicitly quantified literal theorem; relation to any alternative intended formulation must be reconciled. The result is accepted at the exact audited head `56b3a35182e5cb04b05e41f5017e47caf50582c1`. 2 fresh independent complete AI whole-package reviews were completed, with the final review finding zero actionable issues. Subsequent bounded administrative adoption is recorded in the current external ROOT final seal; earlier status/counter/hold fields remain dated history. Prior mathematical results and proof dependencies are credited. Historical novelty and worldwide current openness are unestablished. AI tools were used extensively; this is an unrefereed preprint, without conventional human peer review or formal proof certification. The repository Zenodo uploader verified the exact reviewed metadata and PDF/support bytes. The Google Workspace CLI recorded the DOI/details in the requested tracker with exact read-back. No GitHub release is created. Current audit and publication receipts: `audits/pr1047_30004909`.
Preserved original PR description: dated submission history ## Complete negative result, with precise source scope For problem 30004909 / OWR-8415356-020, this proof-only edition gives a complete obstruction to dimension-independent approximation by one ordinary matroid rank on the same finite ground set. The square-root-cardinality family f(S)=sqrt(|S|) forces alpha >= n^(1/6). The complete manuscript also proves that uniform matroids attain the exact square-root-family optimum min_R max(sqrt(R),sqrt(n)/R), with sharp n^(1/6) for cube n. A rational-valued family on n=m² elements forces alpha²+alpha >= m and alpha >= n^(1/4)/sqrt(2). All claims use one basis/full-ground-set method, approach 1/5. ## Source correction and limits [László Végh's original contribution](https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/46931), Oberwolfach Report 53/2021, printed p. 2946 (PDF page 54), displays r(S)/alpha <= f(S) <= alpha*r(S). The corpus omitted the lower denominator; this proof treats the source-corrected, weaker comparison. The source says constant without separately quantifying over finite ground sets. The edition makes the dimension-independent interpretation explicit. The result concerns a single ordinary rank on the same ground set. It does not address sums of ranks, weighted ranks, expanded ground sets, a scalar-rescaled output class, or an unspecified alternative intended formulation. The square-root-family sharpness is not an optimal exponent claim for all normalized submodular functions. No novelty, historical-priority, exhaustive-literature or prior-current-open-status claim is made. The related Goemans–Harvey–Iwata–Mirrokni oracle-learning problem has a different output class and is not used to infer this result. ## Complete proof and mathematical/source audit REPORT.md is preserved byte-for-byte, including every proof, qualification and source reference. SOURCE_AUDIT.md retains all mathematical checks, original-source observations, literature-search limits and disposition. Only private repository/corpus-history and deduplication details are omitted; the public audit explicitly labels this editorial selection. The selected artifact inventory binds the actual edition documents and omits supplementary computational/private-history identities. A separate complete reading accepted the same mathematical scope. The written proof is self-contained. AI-assisted mathematical/source acceptance is not external human peer review, journal acceptance or formal proof-assistant verification. The bounded literature search did not locate an exact prior presentation of this elementary obstruction; it does not certify novelty. ## Exact additive boundary Add exactly nine files under `unsolved_math_prioritization/attempts/30004909/`. No QUEUE.md or unrelated repository file changes. No executable scripts, fixtures, standalone computational outputs, logs, copied third-party documents, source text, source renderings, datasets, private sources or coordination files are included, and no hashes of those excluded materials are published. Raw public PDF identities and source inspection history are metadata only. Byte checks and clean additive replay establish packaging integrity, not mathematical truth. Draft for review; no merge or release is requested. ## Exact file identities - `ACCEPTANCE.md`: 3,435 bytes; SHA-256 `becf3bf27de2ba42173b92d957b05faeb9ff42b0952691241ef2d24b51be8824` - `ARTIFACT_MANIFEST.json`: 1,159 bytes; SHA-256 `a5358f893734b6baaa90e76b2dc47bc5908ea5f6e62209cfe5e0bdac6ecf9505` - `MANIFEST.json`: 1,843 bytes; SHA-256 `48bee532499f708635ca0ad640c557482c8f9214df0432248ed610645dc5611e` - `PROVENANCE.md`: 4,027 bytes; SHA-256 `3cd88bc109b6311418b491b28f1fd719802e193915c088234612ed711a909480` - `README.md`: 3,104 bytes; SHA-256 `7fbf7dc77f9a905880cec1947fa2eaed4f331ea4d0e28eeb0d2c361d1cdf8eed` - `REPORT.md`: 7,119 bytes; SHA-256 `0e5cc70ca135c8eb9c271ebc65019af92d62e7ade8ff24de5886de9f05721c52` - `SOURCE_AUDIT.md`: 4,728 bytes; SHA-256 `3029a21030ac72d139cc43a90ecad36a79b6a5ce64d92af754a09ad3e6428a5b` - `SOURCE_PROVENANCE.json`: 4,118 bytes; SHA-256 `61a8d2acff818ca071e388a2ebf6c15f51df2eb19cbf4b3894fb6093c279f975` - `STATUS.json`: 2,049 bytes; SHA-256 `4f723f56a90fede76a6a4d55742f0dc29c3fcb798165d1931514f6fa8a32335e` The manifest lists all nine members and hashes the other eight; this body pins the manifest independently.
